note: A read-only decision-graph view was added to nestor ui: a Cytoscape.js (MIT) surface showing decisions as nodes and the four typed relations as edges. Chosen by an explicit two-lens survey first -- a research agent vetted graph/DB viewers against the constraint that this is an Apache-2.0 project and license-VERIFIED each from its own LICENSE/package.json (catching that elkjs, the layout engine most advice reaches for, is EPL/GPL copyleft and not re-landable). Built by one sub-agent in an isolated worktree, then audited: the four security-critical claims were checked by hand -- the CSP header is byte-for-byte unchanged (a viewer that could exfiltrate the memory it displays would defeat the desk's whole point), the two modified self-containment tests were confirmed to be narrowed honestly rather than weakened, and the vendored 435 KB blob was confirmed to be the genuine Cytoscape MIT distribution by sha256 and its own license header, not an error page. Driven for real in Chromium against the 379-decision dogfood store before merge.

decisions.question: Nestor already license-checked a graph viewer for the decision store. How should the read-only Graph tab reach it under a CSP with script-src 'unsafe-inline' and no 'self', and what counts as a 'decision' domain when the store also holds entity and numeric domains with the same tag-shape?
decisions.commitment: Vendor Cytoscape.js 3.34.1 (MIT) at nestor/vendor/, read and inlined into the served page's own inline script at import time -- never a script src=, never a CDN, the CSP left byte-for-byte unchanged and pinned in a regression test. GET /api/graph is a pure read that walks only domains whose tags match 'decision' or 'decision:*' on both sides (the convention DecisionMemory already documents), explicitly excluding any domain that merely happens to share the same-tag-on-both-sides shape (entity, numeric), and returns honestly empty rather than erroring when a store has no decisions or no edge capability.
decisions.why: The CSP is load-bearing -- an audit surface must not be able to exfiltrate the memory it shows -- so 'vendor cleanly and inline the bytes' was the only shape that could work; a CDN or a same-origin script file would both be blocked, and loosening the policy was off the table. The domain-name convention (rather than inferring 'is this a decision?' from tag shape) was the only way to avoid dressing up an entity alias or a reconciled figure as a decision that no human ever proposed as one -- pinned by an adversarial test that a store's entity and numeric domains never leak into the graph. The viewer seals nothing and has no write path: /api/graph is GET-only, so a mutation attempt is a plain 404, not a checked-and-refused write.
decisions.doors_closed: No elkjs (EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0 -- copyleft, verified from its package.json, not re-landable into an Apache-2.0 project). No cytoscape-dagre -- the built-in breadthfirst layout sufficed, so the optional MIT dependency was not taken. No capability inference from tag shape alone. Follow-up noted, not done: a disconnected all-draft corpus renders as a row under breadthfirst -- a layout better suited to disconnected nodes would read better once there are seals and edges to show.
